observations: Photo 0: A TV screen shows the PlayStation 5 interface with game icons including FC25, Call of Duty, and others. Below the TV, a silver, vertically oriented console is visible, wrapped in plastic. The console is placed on a black stand. A watermark 'JAYCYBER GAMES' is visible on the screen.
Photo 1: The same TV screen now displays the FC25 game menu. The silver console is still visible below, wrapped in plastic. The same watermark is present.
Photo 2: The TV screen again shows the PlayStation 5 game library, identical to photo 0. The silver console remains wrapped in plastic below the TV. The watermark is still visible.
The console appears to be a PlayStation 5 Disc Edition (‘fat’ model) based on its vertical orientation, silver color, and design, though no branding is visible on the console itself.
The console is wrapped in plastic, suggesting it may be new or recently unboxed.
The TV screen shows the PS5 interface, indicating the console is powered on and functional at the time of the photo.
No physical games or game cases are visible in any photo.
The seller claims 'never been fixed' — likely meaning 'never been repaired' — but this cannot be verified remotely.

claims.evidence: The console's vertical orientation, silver color, and design in photos 0, 1, and 2 match the PlayStation 5 Disc Edition (‘fat’ model). The interface on the TV screen confirms it is a PS5.
The TV screen shows installed games (FC25, Call of Duty, etc.), but no physical game cases or discs are visible in any photo. The games may be digital downloads.
There is no visual evidence to confirm or deny whether the console has been repaired. The plastic wrap suggests it may be new, but this does not prove it has never been fixed.

risks.risk: Console may be non-functional or have hidden hardware issues
risks.proof: A video showing the console powering on, booting into the system, and playing a game for 30 seconds.

risks.risk: Games are digital only, not physical copies as implied
risks.proof: Photos of physical game cases or discs, or a screenshot showing the game library with digital download status.
risks.if_unproven: priced as no physical games included

risks.risk: Console may be stolen or cloned (e.g., fake or unauthorized unit)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the console's serial number and a video of the console being powered on and showing the system settings screen with the serial number.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the console's front and back, showing the brand and model name.
A video of the console powering on, booting into the system, and playing a game for 30 seconds.
Photos of any physical game cases or discs, if available.
A clear photo of the console's serial number.
response.reason: The console appears to be a PlayStation 5 Disc Edition based on the interface and design, but critical details such as physical games, functionality, and authenticity cannot be confirmed from the current photos. The claim of 'never been fixed' is unverifiable remotely. Proof is needed to assess functionality, game type, and authenticity before pricing.
